prompt: Tell me about a time you were really scared/embarrassed/angry
speech1: I recall... well, it was years ago when the storm hit the coast. We were... we were quite isolated out there on the point. I kept checking the windows and... everything seemed so dark and loud. It took me a long time to... to find the right words to calm the children down. I remember feeling very small against the wind.
speech2: Oh my gosh, okay, so this one time I was at this fancy wedding, you know, and I totally tripped! I was like, carrying two glasses of punch and just—whoosh—down I went, haha! It was so bad because the music just stopped right as I hit the floor, right? Everyone was looking, and I just started laughing because, honestly, what else can you do? I’m always doing stuff like that, just rushing around and not looking where my feet are going!
speech3: I remember feeling so... well, it was a deep kind of anger, though looking back it feels softer now. My daughter had decided to move so far away, and I... I suppose I wasn't ready to let go of our Sundays together. It wasn't really about her choice, it was more about... anyway, I said some things I didn't mean. I wish I could go back to that kitchen table and just... just hold her hand instead of shouting. Sometimes our hearts get ahead of our heads, don't they?
speech4: I was working in the shop and the table saw kicked back a piece of oak right toward my chest. It missed by an inch, and for a second, I realized exactly how dangerous that machine actually is. I didn't panic or anything, but I definitely felt a cold chill go down my spine. I turned the power off, took a five-minute break, and went back to finish the job. There isn't much point in dwelling on what might have happened when you have work to do.
speech5: The fog had rolled in so thick you couldn't see your own hand stretched out in front of your face. I was walking the old creek path when the most blood-curdling screech echoed through the pines, stopping me dead in my tracks. Every hair on my neck stood up as the woods went silent, waiting for whatever beast had made that sound to move again. My heart was thumping against my ribs like a trapped bird, and I didn't dare breathe for what felt like an eternity. It was only a great horned owl taking flight, but in that moment, the shadows felt alive and hungry.
